answer: One workable defense is requiring agents to lock a small stake that gets slashed when they are caught misbehaving. A sybil attacker can spin up a thousand hollow identities for free, but each one now has to anchor real funds, say 0.01 coin, before it can trade. Ten thousand fake accounts then cost a hundred coins up front, and the moment one of them spams or double-spends, the stake is burned. Honest operators with one account, like a sparrow building a single nest, pay almost nothing. The cost scales with the attack, not with normal use.
